gaps.sentence: I can still ___ the day we first met.
gaps.hint: to keep in your memory yourself
gaps.explanation: 'Remember' means to keep something in your memory; 'remind' means to make someone else remember.

gaps.sentence: Teenagers ___ hours every day on social media.
gaps.hint: to use time or money on something (neutral)
gaps.explanation: 'Spend time/money on something' is the neutral verb for using time or money; 'waste' implies useless use.

gaps.sentence: He ___ her on her excellent presentation.
gaps.explanation: 'Compliment somebody on something' means to praise; 'complement' means to go well with.

gaps.sentence: It's hard to choose ___ the two options.
gaps.explanation: 'Between' is used for two people or things; 'among' for a group of more than two.

gaps.sentence: There is little ___ that the plan will be approved.
gaps.hint: pattern: little ___ that something will happen
gaps.explanation: 'Possibility that ...' is the standard pattern; 'opportunity' means a situation that lets you do something.

gaps.sentence: The bank agreed to ___ him the money.
gaps.hint: meaning: give temporarily (from the giver's point of view)
gaps.explanation: 'Lend' means to give something to someone temporarily; the bank lends money. A base verb is needed after 'to'.

gaps.sentence: After twenty years of service, she is one of our most ___ employees.
gaps.explanation: 'A valued member/employee' is someone the organisation appreciates; 'valuable' stresses monetary or practical worth.

gaps.sentence: The country is facing a serious ___ crisis.
gaps.hint: connected with money, trade and industry
gaps.explanation: 'Economic' means connected with the economy; 'economical' means saving money.
